summary: 1921 lookout camp, 1930 log cabin, 1937 L-4 cab destroyed in 1969. A WillhiteWeb photo caption mentions a footing; a trail closure notice dated 7.30.26 is posted.

facts.design: Log cabin with a roof platform (1930), replaced by an L-4 cab (1937); a 1950 USGS description gives a 14-foot-square wooden building on the ground

staffing.status: Arnold Hagen named as a lookout in 1933; no later staffing in the sources read

access.note: Hikers can reach the mountain on Wenatchee National Forest trails. Passenger cars cannot reach the Cougar Ridge trailhead. WTA posted a closure notice dated 7.30.26 because of the Little Giant Fire.

visit.trail_note: Roughly 5 miles one way from Maverick Saddle per WillhiteWeb; WTA lists a 10-mile round trip. Check for closures before going.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Wenatchee National Forest
facts.status_note: The L-4 cab was destroyed in 1969; a WillhiteWeb photo caption mentions a footing under the ground. No source describes the site now.

corrections.why: 4.3 m is 14 feet, the square width the 1950 USGS description gives for the building. The same description puts the V-type roof about 12 feet (3.7 m) above the ground. Reviewer to confirm the intended height or drop the field, since no source gives height to the cab floor.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Former Fire Lookout Sites page says the L-4 cab was removed in 1969; WillhiteWeb and the Fire Lookout page say destroyed in 1969. The story uses destroyed and notes the register's word. No source explains how the cab was lost.

notes_for_editor: Access: the WTA closure notice is dated 7.30.26 and the cached page may be out of date. Check the current closure before anyone advises a visit. Two approaches are described: the Forest Service's Cougar Ridge Trail behind gated Forest Road 5700, and WillhiteWeb's route from Maverick Saddle up the Mad River Trail. The footing caption is undated. The record's height_m 4.3 appears to be the 14-foot building width, so a correction is proposed rather than applied. WTA lists its hike as Cougar Mountain (#1415), while the Forest Service calls the Cougar Ridge Trail #1418 and says it ends at Tyee Ridge Trail #1415, so the WTA closure may not cover the Cougar Ridge route; the story now names the WTA hike.
